clue.text: Use bread to soak up savoury dish

parts.note: a roll is a small loaf of bread
to mop is to soak up liquid with a cloth or sponge

explanation.surface: Advice to wipe up a tasty plate's juices with a piece of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use' and 'to' are only link words here. A rollmop is a rolled pickled herring fillet, a common British deli item.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a pickled herring fillet rolled around onion, eaten as a savoury snack or starter.

clue.text: Actor's plush Tudor barn gets damaged

definitions.note: the possessive 's joins the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: plush means luxurious, rich

indicators.note: damaged words are knocked out of shape, so the letters of Tudor barn are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film star's luxurious old Tudor barn has suffered some damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Burton was a celebrated Welsh stage and screen actor.

clue.text: She may be tricky to alter

indicators.note: something tricky is twisty and awkward, so the letters of to alter are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman is said to be difficult when it comes to making changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Loretta is a woman's name, and the definition simply points to any female person.

clue.text: Apparently cis one chapter in notes

clue.text: Valuable substance symbolically displayed in centre of receptacle

definitions.text: Valuable substance symbolically displayed in centre of receptacle

parts.words: Valuable substance symbolically displayed in centre of receptacle
parts.note: the precious metal whose chemical symbol, Pt, sits at the very middle of the word receptacle

explanation.surface: A treasure kept on show in the middle of a container.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle two letters of RECEPTACLE are P and T, and Pt is this metal's chemical symbol, so the clue describes the metal by where its symbol appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum is a precious metal, valuable for jewellery and catalysts, with the chemical symbol Pt.

clue.text: Give popularity to organ, one's first aim

indicators.note: says the aim word is placed first, before the organ

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Advice on promoting a musical instrument by putting it first.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear someone to others is to make them liked, giving them popularity.

clue.text: Book model to show up

parts.note: Ex is the usual short form of Exodus, a book of the Bible
to pose is to model for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: Hiring someone to sit for a portrait so they can appear.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone up is to reveal their faults, which is to expose them.

clue.text: Medic's extremely unbalanced memory, a realistic fiction

parts.note: a doc is a doctor, a medic

indicators.note: the extremes of the word unbalanced are its first and last letters

parts.note: RAM is computer memory

explanation.surface: A doctor's lopsided recollection turns out to be a lifelike work of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A docudrama is a dramatised film of real events, fiction made to look realistic.

clue.text: A call-girl in port

parts.note: in cards a call is a bid
Jan is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A prostitute working in a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Abidjan is the chief port and largest city of Ivory Coast.

clue.text: Has he the heart to cheat ?

definitions.text: Has he the heart to cheat ?

parts.words: Has he the heart to cheat ?
parts.note: a heart is a playing card, and a sharp is a cheat, so the question reads as asking about a card-table cheat

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a man is cruel enough to deceive someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a swindler who cheats at card games, and hearts are a suit of cards.

clue.text: Carbineer regularly a court official

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every other one from the word Carbineer

explanation.surface: An armed soldier who doubles as an officer of the law court.
explanation.definitionFit: A crier is an official who makes announcements in a court of law.

clue.text: Will character let brothers change first?

indicators.note: the rearranged brothers come first, before the synonym for let
the letters of brothers are changed into a new order

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A will that lets brothers alter the order of inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: Will here is William Shakespeare, so a Will character is one of his creations: Robert Shallow is the country justice in Henry IV Part 2.
explanation.definitionFit: Justice Robert Shallow is a comic figure in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2 and The Merry Wives of Windsor.

clue.text: Grotesque worker in charge

parts.note: the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: An ugly labourer put in control.
explanation.definitionFit: Antic as an adjective means grotesque or bizarre in a clownish way.

clue.text: Type of crime where Jacob conceals bill?

definitions.text: Type of crime where Jacob conceals bill?

parts.words: Type of crime where Jacob conceals bill?
parts.note: a bill is an account, AC, and JACOB holds AC with JOB around it, so the bill is within a job

explanation.surface: Asking what sort of offence it is when a man hides an invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: AC is the usual short form of account, another word for a bill; remove it from JACOB and JOB is left around it.
explanation.definitionFit: An inside job is a crime committed by, or with help from, someone within the targeted organisation.

clue.text: Fungus on curtains starts to create unholy pong

parts.note: curtains is slang for the end, death

indicators.note: the starts of the next three words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Mould on the drapes is beginning to make a dreadful smell.
explanation.definitionFit: The death cap is a deadly poisonous mushroom, a kind of fungus.

clue.text: Consecrated wine, about a litre — it's blooming great

indicators.note: the word for consecrated goes around the litre

parts.note: consecrated means holy
L is the abbreviation for a litre
hock is a white wine from the Rhine region of Germany

explanation.surface: Holy wine, about a litre's worth, which is really excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming great' sounds like British slang for very good, but it means a tall flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollyhock is a tall garden plant with large flowers, so it is both in bloom and big.

clue.text: Bearing heavenly food, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: manna is the food sent from heaven in the Bible

explanation.surface: Carrying celestial nourishment, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's bearing is their way of carrying themselves, their manner.

clue.text: Like glass, flexibly supportive, but not very soft

indicators.note: flexibly bent into another shape, so the letters of supportive are rearranged

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very soft

explanation.surface: Something glassy that bends to support, though not gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes PP from SUPPORTIVE, and 'flexibly' rearranges the remaining letters SUORTIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitreous means glassy, having the look or nature of glass.

clue.text: In France one's aged and left on the shelf

parts.note: un is French for one, with the possessive s
aged means old

explanation.surface: A Frenchman who is elderly and still single.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods left on the shelf have not been bought, so they are unsold.

clue.text: Observer of artist such as Seurat?

definitions.meaning: one who spots or watches things
Seurat painted in tiny dots of colour, so playfully he puts spots on canvas

explanation.definitionFit: A spotter watches for things, and Seurat's pointillism laid paint down in spots.

clue.text: Grand love affairs, but not right to have such a marriage?

parts.note: grand means big

indicators.note: says the letter for right is removed

parts.note: amours are love affairs

explanation.surface: Big romances, though wrong to enter such a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigamous marriage is one entered while already married to someone else.

clue.text: Exit for the open air

definitions.meaning: a way out, a door leading outside
taking place outside rather than indoors

explanation.definitionFit: An out door is a door leading out, and outdoor describes things done outside.

clue.text: At front of boat, shortly discover fish

parts.note: the bow is the front of a boat

indicators.note: cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: to discover is to find

explanation.surface: At the bow of a boat, soon finding a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The bowfin is a primitive freshwater fish of North America.

clue.text: The number of hours in a day a carpenter might work ?

definitions.text: The number of hours in a day a carpenter might work ?

parts.words: The number of hours in a day a carpenter might work ?
parts.note: a day has twenty-four hours, which as a multiplication is two times four, and carpenters work with timber of that size

explanation.surface: A question about how long a woodworker spends at work each day.
explanation.walkthrough: The 24 hours in a day can be read as 2 x 4, which is the name of a standard timber size.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-by-four is a length of timber two inches by four in cross-section, a carpenter's stock material.

clue.text: Vestment is Catholic's first outrageous article

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means outrageous
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A church garment described as a Catholic's most outlandish item.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotta is a short surplice, a vestment worn in church.

clue.text: In stone, a firm overhead rib

indicators.note: the abbreviation for stone goes inside the other letters
in a down clue the firm sits above the a

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
st is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: A ridge carved overhead in stonework by a building company.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa is the anatomical Latin term for a rib.

clue.text: Sportingly held back some explosive material

indicators.note: held back means the letters are read in reverse order
some of the word Sportingly is taken

explanation.surface: A sporting gesture restrains a dangerous amount of explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitro is short for nitroglycerine, a powerful liquid explosive.

clue.text: The rest of the plates?

parts.note: plates of meat is Cockney rhyming slang for feet, so a rest for them

explanation.surface: Asking what remains of the crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang plates of meat means feet, so 'plates' are feet and 'rest' is something to rest them on.
explanation.definitionFit: A footstool is a low stool for resting the feet on.

clue.text: Turn vessel, understanding there's a monster at sea

indicators.note: turning the word for vessel round reads it backwards

parts.note: an ark is a vessel, as Noah's
ken means knowledge or understanding

explanation.surface: Steering a ship round, knowing a sea beast is lurking.
explanation.definitionFit: The kraken is a legendary giant sea monster of Scandinavian folklore.

clue.text: Fight and argue with one on the wing

parts.note: to spar is to fight, box
to row is to quarrel, argue

explanation.surface: Boxing and quarrelling with a player out on the wing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparrow is a small bird, something that flies on the wing.
